last_tool.excerpt: CORROBORATION Definition & Meaning | Dictionary.com Featured Games Cultural Writing tips Dictionary.com Thesaurus.com Definition Other Word Forms Etymology Explanation Lists Examples Related Words Synonyms corroboration American [k uh -rob- uh - rey -sh uh n] / kəˌrɒb əˈreɪ ʃən / noun the act of corroborating . a corroboratory fact, statement, etc. Other Word Forms noncorroboration noun Etymology Origin of corroboration 1425–75; late Middle English ( corroborātiōn- (stem of corroborātiō ). See corroborate , -ion Explanation If you tell your boss you couldn't go to work because you were sick and then produce a doctor's note, that's corroboration — a fancy term for "evidence" — something that backs up a statement or a theory. Corroboration is probably the kind of word you wouldn't use in casual conversation; you would more likely use proof , for example. It's generally used in a more technical or formal sense, regarding a legal case, perhaps, or a scientific experiment, as in: "Physicists today are finding increasing corroboration that Einstein's theories were correct."
